`GET /v2/calendar/{market}`

This endpoint returns the market calendar.

<h3 id="get-market-calendar-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|market|path|[market](#schemamarket)|true|The market identifier. MIC, BIC, or acronym.<br><br>Available market codes by region:<br><br>**United States**<br>- `BMO`: Bank of Montreal. US banking calendar (US operations).<br>- `BNYM`: The Bank of New York Mellon. US banking calendar.<br>- `BOATS`: Blue Ocean Alternative Trading System. US overnight trading.<br>- `IEX`: Investors Exchange. US equities.<br>- `IEXG`: Investors Exchange. US equities.<br>- `NASDAQ`: National Association of Securities Dealers Automated Quotations. US equities.<br>- `NYSE`: New York Stock Exchange. US equities.<br>- `OCEA`: BlueOcean ATS. US overnight trading.<br>- `OPRA`: Options Price Reporting Authority. US options.<br>- `OTC`: Over-The-Counter. US OTC equities.<br>- `OTCM`: OTC Markets. US OTC equities.<br>- `SIFMA`: Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association. US bonds.<br>- `XNAS`: NASDAQ. US equities.<br>- `XNYS`: New York Stock Exchange. US equities.<br><br>**Europe**<br>- `CEUX`: Cboe CEUX Europe. European equities (Cboe Netherlands).<br>- `CHIX`: Cboe CHIX Europe. European equities (Cboe UK).<br>- `ISE`: Euronext Dublin. Irish equities.<br>- `LSE`: London Stock Exchange. UK equities.<br>- `MTA`: Euronext Milan. Italian equities.<br>- `MTAA`: Euronext Milan. Italian equities.<br>- `XAMS`: Euronext Amsterdam. Dutch equities.<br>- `XBRU`: Euronext Brussels. Belgian equities.<br>- `XDUB`: Euronext Dublin. Irish equities.<br>- `XETR`: Frankfurt Stock Exchange. German equities.<br>- `XETRA`: Frankfurt Stock Exchange. German equities.<br>- `XLIS`: Euronext Lisbon. Portuguese equities.<br>- `XLON`: London Stock Exchange. UK equities.<br>- `XPAR`: Euronext Paris. French equities.<br><br>**Asia & Middle East**<br>- `HKEX`: Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Hong Kong equities.<br>- `JPX`: Japan Exchange Group. Japanese equities.<br>- `TADAWUL`: Saudi Stock Exchange. Saudi equities.<br>- `XHKG`: Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Hong Kong equities.<br>- `XSAU`: Saudi Stock Exchange. Saudi equities.<br>- `XTKS`: Japan Exchange Group. Japanese equities.<br>|
|start|query|string(date)|false|The first date to retrieve data for (inclusive). Default: today.<br>|
|end|query|string(date)|false|The last date to retrieve data for (inclusive). Default: one week from the start date.<br>|
|timezone|query|string|false|Timezone of the times. Default: the timezone of the market.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|market|BMO|

## Subscribe to Account Status Events (SSE)

<a id="opIdsubscribeToAccountStatusSSE"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/events/accounts/status \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/events/accounts/status`

The accounts events API provides streaming of account changes as they occur, via SSE (server sent events). Past events can also be queried.

Events are generated for changes to the following account properties:
- account_blocked
- admin_configurations
- cash_interest
- crypto_status
- kyc_results
- options
- status
- trading_blocked

Only the changed properties are included in the event payload.

Query Parameter Rules:
- `since_id` and `until_id` are deprecated and available only to select broker partners; use `since_ulid` and `until_ulid` instead
- `since` is required if `until` specified
- `since_id` is required if `until_id` specified
- `since_ulid` is required if `until_ulid` specified
- `since`, `since_id` and `since_ulid` can't be used at the same time

Behavior:
This API supports querying a range of events, starting now or in the past. If the end of the range is in the future or not specified, the connection is kept open and future events are pushed.

To be specific:
- if `since`, `since_id` or `since_ulid` is not specified, this will not return any historic data
- if `until`, `until_id` or `until_ulid` is reached, the stream will end with a status of 200

---

Note for people using the clients generated from this OAS spec. Currently OAS-3 doesn't have full support for representing SSE style responses from an API, so if you are using a generated client and don't specify a `since` and `until` there is a good chance the generated clients will hang waiting for the response to end.

If you require the streaming capabilities we recommend not using the generated clients for this specific usecase until the OAS-3 standards come to a consensus on how to represent this correctly in OAS-3.


<h3 id="subscribe-to-account-status-events-sse-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|string(date)|false|Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|until|query|string(date)|false|Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|since_id|query|integer|false|**Deprecated.** **Deprecation notice:**<br>Use since_ulid instead.<br><br>Since: 2023-08-01<br>Sunset: 2027-02-15|
|until_id|query|integer|false|**Deprecated.** **Deprecation notice:**<br>Use until_ulid instead.<br><br>Since: 2023-08-01<br>Sunset: 2027-02-15|
|since_ulid|query|string(ulid)|false|none|
|until_ulid|query|string(ulid)|false|none|
|id|query|string|false|none|

<h3 id="subscribe-to-account-status-events-sse-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Connected. Events will now start streaming as long as you keep the connection open.|Inline|

<h3 id="subscribe-to-account-status-events-sse-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[AccountStatusEvent](#schemaaccountstatusevent)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Subscribe to Journal Events (SSE) (Legacy)

<a id="opIdsubscribeToJournalStatusSSE"></a>

  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/events/journals/status`

The Events API provides event push as well as historical queries via SSE (server sent events).

You can listen to journal status updates as they get processed by our backoffice.

Historical events are streamed immediately if queried, and updates are pushed as events occur.

Query Params Rules:
- `since_id` and `until_id` are deprecated and available only to select broker partners; use `since_ulid` and `until_ulid` instead
- `since` required if `until` specified
- `since_id` required if `until_id` specified
- `since_ulid` required if `until_ulid` specified
- `since`, `since_id` or `since_ulid`  can't be used at the same time
Behavior:
- if `since`, `since_id` or `since_ulid` not specified this will not return any historic data
- if `until`, `until_id` or `until_ulid` reached stream will end (status 200)

---

There is no compatibility between /v1/events/journals/status and /v2/events/journals/status, the ids (ulid) are always different, and the number of events might also different

Please note that the new `/v2` endpoint, is the same as, and was originally available under `/v2beta1`.
We encourage all customers to adjust their codebase from that interim beta endpoint to the `/v2` stable endpoint.
In the near future we will setup permanent redirect from `/v2beta1` to `/v2` before we completely remove the beta endpoint.

---

Note for people using the clients generated from this OAS spec. Currently OAS-3 doesn't have full support for representing SSE style responses from an API, so if you are using a generated client and don't specify a `since` and `until` there is a good chance the generated clients will hang waiting for the response to end.

If you require the streaming capabilities we recommend not using the generated clients for this specific usecase until the OAS-3 standards come to a consensus on how to represent this correctly in OAS-3.

## Subscribe to Activity Events (SSE)

<a id="opIdsubscribeToActivitiesSSE"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v2beta1/events/activities \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v2beta1/events/activities`

The Events API sends the real-time events and provides historical queries with SSE (Server Sent Events).

This endpoint streams events on account activities.

Historical events are streamed immediately if queried, and updates are pushed as events occur.

Query parameter rules:
- If `until` is specified, `since` is required.
- If `until_id` is specified, `since_id` is required.
- You cannot use `since` and `since_id` together.
Behavior:
- If `since` or `since_id` is not specified, this will not return any historic data.
- If `until` or `until_id` is specified, stream will end at the specified point with status 200.

---

Warning: Currently, OAS-3 does not fully support responses from an SSE API.

In case the client code is generated from this OAS spec, please do not specify `since` and `until`, as the generated client may hang forever waiting for the response to end.

If you require the streaming capabilities, we recommend not using the generated clients for this specific endpoint until the OAS-3 standards define how to represent this behavior.

---

###  Comment messages
According to the SSE specification, any line that starts with a colon is a comment which does not contain data.  It is typically a free text that does not follow any data schema. A few examples mentioned below for comment messages.

#####  Slow client

The server sends a comment when the client is not consuming messages fast enough. Example: `: you are reading too slowly, dropped 10000 messages`

##### Internal server error

An error message is sent as a comment when the server closes the connection on an internal server error (only sent by the v2 and v2beta1 endpoints). Example: `: internal server error`

---

<h3 id="subscribe-to-activity-events-sse-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Format: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|Format: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD|
|since_id|query|string(ulid)|false|none|
|until_id|query|string(ulid)|false|none|

<h3 id="subscribe-to-activity-events-sse-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Connected. Events will now start streaming as long as you keep the connection open.|Inline|

<h3 id="subscribe-to-activity-events-sse-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|*anonymous*|[[ActivityEventV2](#schemaactivityeventv2)]|false|none|none|

`GET /v2/events/admin-actions`

The Events API provides event push as well as historical queries via SSE (server sent events).

This endpoint streams events related to administrative actions performed by our systems.

Historical events are streamed immediately if queried, and updates are pushed as events occur.

Query Params Rules:
- `since` required if `until` specified
- `since_id` required if `until_id` specified

###  Comment messages
According to the SSE specification, any line that starts with a colon is a comment which does not contain data.  It is typically a free text that does not follow any data schema. A few examples mentioned below for comment messages.

#####  Slow client

The server sends a comment when the client is not consuming messages fast enough. Example: `: you are reading too slowly, dropped 10000 messages`

##### Internal server error

An error message is sent as a comment when the server closes the connection on an internal server error (only sent by the v2 and v2beta1 endpoints). Example: `: internal server error`

**Event Types**

- **LegacyNote:** Old free text based admin notes
- **Liquidation:** Event for a position liquidation which initialized by an admin
- **TransactionCancel:** Event for a manually cancelled transaction
- **AcatsStatus:** Event for a status change of an ACATS transfer (`type: acats_status_admin_event`, `category: acats`). Only sent to correspondents with ACATS API access.

## Subscribe to IPO Events (SSE)

<a id="opIdsubscribeToIPOEventsSSE"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v2/events/ipos \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v2/events/ipos`

The Events API provides event push as well as historical queries via SSE (server sent events).

You can listen to IPO offering lifecycle updates as they happen - including new offerings, offering updates, prospectus availability, the 60-minute pricing window, account-scoped allocation results, and offering cancellations.

Historical events are streamed immediately if queried, and updates are pushed as events occur.

---

**Event types**

Each event has a `verb` field that determines the shape of `payload`. See the `IPOEvent` schema for the full payload structure for each verb.

- `Offering` - initial publication of an offering (system-wide).
- `OfferingUpdate` - update to a previously published offering (system-wide).
- `Prospectus` - prospectus document is now available (system-wide).
- `SixtyMinMail` - 60-minute pricing window has opened, no new orders accepted (system-wide).
- `Allocation` - final allocation result for a specific account. **Account-scoped** - `account_id` and `correspondent` are populated.
- `OfferingCancellation` - offering was cancelled. **No `payload` field is present.**

Use the `offering_reference` field on each event to fetch the full offering metadata via [`GET /v1/ipos/{offering_reference}`](#operation/getIPOOffering).

---

Query Params Rules:
- `since` required if `until` specified
- `since_id` required if `until_id` specified
- `since` and `since_id` can't be used at the same time
- `until` and `until_id` can't be used at the same time

Behavior:
- if `since` or `since_id` not specified this will not return any historic data
- if `until` or `until_id` reached stream will end (status 200)

---

Note for people using the clients generated from this OAS spec. Currently OAS-3 doesn't have full support for representing SSE style responses from an API, so if you are using a generated client and don't specify a `since` and `until` there is a good chance the generated clients will hang waiting for the response to end.

If you require the streaming capabilities we recommend not using the generated clients for this specific usecase until the OAS-3 standards come to a consensus on how to represent this correctly in OAS-3.


<h3 id="subscribe-to-ipo-events-sse-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|string(date-time)|false|Format: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD|
|until|query|string(date-time)|false|Format: RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD|
|since_id|query|string(ulid)|false|ULID `event_id` to resume the stream from. The first event returned will be the one immediately after `since_id`.|
|until_id|query|string(ulid)|false|ULID `event_id` at which the stream will end (inclusive). Useful for backfills.|

## Subscribe to Trade Events (SSE)

<a id="opIdsubscribeToTradeV2SSE"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v2/events/trades \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v2/events/trades`

The Events API provides event push as well as historical queries via SSE (server sent events).

You can listen to events related to trade updates. Most market trades sent during market hours are filled instantly; you can listen to limit order updates through this endpoint.

Historical events are streamed immediately if queried, and updates are pushed as events occur.

Query Params Rules:
- `since` required if `until` specified
- `since_id` required if `until_id` specified
- `since` and `since_id` can't be used at the same time
Behavior:
- if `since` or `since_id` not specified this will not return any historic data
- if `until` or `until_id` reached stream will end (status 200)

---

Note for people using the clients generated from this OAS spec. Currently OAS-3 doesn't have full support for representing SSE style responses from an API, so if you are using a generated client and don't specify a `since` and `until` there is a good chance the generated clients will hang waiting for the response to end.

If you require the streaming capabilities we recommend not using the generated clients for this specific usecase until the OAS-3 standards come to a consensus on how to represent this correctly in OAS-3.

---

**Legacy trade events API deprecation**

The legacy v1 trade events endpoint has been fully deprecated and is no longer available. Use `/v2/events/trades` for all trade event integrations.

---

###  Comment messages
According to the SSE specification, any line that starts with a colon is a comment which does not contain data.  It is typically a free text that does not follow any data schema. A few examples mentioned below for comment messages.

#####  Slow client

The server sends a comment when the client is not consuming messages fast enough. Example: `: you are reading too slowly, dropped 10000 messages`

##### Internal server error

An error message is sent as a comment when the server closes the connection on an internal server error (only sent by the v2 and v2beta1 endpoints). Example: `: internal server error`

---

**Common events**

These are the events that are the expected results of actions you may have taken by sending API requests.

The meaning of the timestamp field changes for each type; the meanings have been specified here for which types the timestamp field will be present.

- `accepted` Sent when an order is received and accepted by Alpaca
- `pending_new` Sent when the order has been received by Alpaca and routed to the exchanges, but has not yet been accepted for execution.
- `new` Sent when an order has been routed to exchanges for execution.
- `fill` Sent when your order has been completely filled.
  - timestamp: The time at which the order was filled.
- `partial_fill` Sent when a number of shares less than the total remaining quantity on your order has been filled.
  - timestamp: The time at which the shares were filled.
- `canceled` Sent when your requested cancellation of an order is processed.
  - timestamp: The time at which the order was canceled.
- `expired` Sent when an order has reached the end of its lifespan, as determined by the order's time in force value.
  - timestamp: The time at which the order expired.
- `done_for_day` Sent when the order is done executing for the day, and will not receive further updates until the next trading day.
- `replaced` Sent when your requested replacement of an order is processed.
  - timestamp: The time at which the order was replaced.

**Rarer events**

These are events that may rarely be sent due to unexpected circumstances on the exchanges. It is unlikely you will need to design your code around them, but you may still wish to account for the possibility that they will occur.

- `rejected` Sent when your order has been rejected.
  - timestamp: The time at which the rejection occurred.
- `held` For multi-leg orders, the secondary orders (stop loss, take profit) will enter this state while waiting to be triggered.
- `stopped` Sent when your order has been stopped, and a trade is guaranteed for the order, usually at a stated price or better, but has not yet occurred.
- `pending_cancel` Sent when the order is awaiting cancellation. Most cancellations will occur without the order entering this state.
- `pending_replace` Sent when the order is awaiting replacement.
- `calculated` Sent when the order has been completed for the day - it is either filled or done_for_day - but remaining settlement calculations are still pending.
- `suspended` Sent when the order has been suspended and is not eligible for trading.
- `order_replace_rejected` Sent when the order replace has been rejected.
- `order_cancel_rejected` Sent when the order cancel has been rejected.
- `trade_bust`: Sent when a previously reported execution has been canceled ("busted") by the upstream exchange.
- `trade_correct`: Sent when a previously reported trade has been corrected. For example, the exchange may have updated the price, quantity, or another execution parameter after the trade was initially reported.
- `restated`: Sent when the order is manually modified.

<h3 id="subscribe-to-trade-events-sse-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|since|query|string(date)|false|Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|until|query|string(date)|false|Format: YYYY-MM-DD|
|since_id|query|string(ulid)|false|none|
|until_id|query|string(ulid)|false|none|

## Request a New Transfer

<a id="opIdcreateTransferForAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/transfers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "additional_information": "string",
    "amount": "string",
    "bank_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "direction": "INCOMING",
    "fee_payment_method": "string",
    "ira": {
      "distribution_reason": "normal",
      "tax_withholding": {
        "fed_pct": "10.25",
        "state_pct": "8.25"
      },
      "tax_year": "2024"
    },
    "relationship_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
    "transfer_type": "ach"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/transfers`

Create a new transfer to deposit money into or withdraw money from an account.

Two `transfer_type` values are accepted, and both are available in sandbox and production:

- **`ach`** — supports both `INCOMING` (deposit) and `OUTGOING` (withdrawal) directions. A `relationship_id` from a previously created [ACH Relationship](https://docs.alpaca.markets/reference/createachrelationshipforaccount) is required.
- **`wire`** — supports the `OUTGOING` (withdrawal) direction only. Incoming wires cannot be initiated through this endpoint; they are pushed in by the sending bank and recorded automatically. A `bank_id` from a previously created [Bank Relationship](https://docs.alpaca.markets/reference/createrecipientbank) is required, and the bank must be in `APPROVED` status before the transfer will progress past `QUEUED`.

In the sandbox environment, ACH deposits and withdrawals settle instantly against virtual funds. Outgoing wire withdrawals are accepted and simulated end-to-end — no funds are transmitted to a bank, but the transfer progresses to `COMPLETE` and the account is debited against virtual funds. Sandbox wire withdrawals are asynchronous (not instant) and auto-complete on weekdays only; transfers submitted on a weekend will not progress until Monday. For more on funding accounts in sandbox, see [this tutorial](https://alpaca.markets/learn/fund-broker-api/).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "additional_information": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "bank_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "direction": "INCOMING",
  "fee_payment_method": "string",
  "ira": {
    "distribution_reason": "normal",
    "tax_withholding": {
      "fed_pct": "10.25",
      "state_pct": "8.25"
    },
    "tax_year": "2024"
  },
  "relationship_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "transfer_type": "ach"
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-new-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string(uuid)|true|none|
|body|body|[CreateTransferRequest](#schemacreatetransferrequest)|true|none|
|» additional_information|body|string \| null|false|Additional details for when type = `wire`|
|» amount|body|string(decimal)|true|Must be > 0.00|
|» bank_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Required if type = `wire`<br><br>The bank_relationship created for the account_id [here](https://alpaca.markets/docs/api-references/broker-api/funding/bank/#creating-a-new-bank-relationship)|
|» direction|body|[TransferDirection](#schematransferdirection)|true|- **INCOMING**<br>Funds incoming to user's account (deposit).<br>- **OUTGOING**<br>Funds outgoing from user's account (withdrawal).<br>|
|» fee_payment_method|body|[FeePaymentMethod](#schemafeepaymentmethod)|false|Only outgoing wire fees are currently supported for automated processing.<br><br><br>**user**	The end user will pay any applicable fees<br>**invoice**	Any applicable fees will be billed to the client in the following monthly invoice|
|» ira|body|[TransferIRA](#schematransferira)|false|This field is used for IRA Account only|
|» relationship_id|body|string(uuid)|false|Required if type = `ach`<br><br>The ach_relationship created for the account_id [here](https://alpaca.markets/docs/api-references/broker-api/funding/ach/#creating-an-ach-relationship)|
|» transfer_type|body|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|- **ach**<br>Transfer via ACH (US Only). Supports both `INCOMING` (deposit) and `OUTGOING` (withdrawal) directions.<br>- **wire**<br>Transfer via wire. `OUTGOING` (withdrawal) only.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» direction|INCOMING|
|» direction|OUTGOING|
|» transfer_type|ach|
|» transfer_type|wire|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "account_id": "449e7a5c-69d3-4b8a-aaaf-5c9b713ebc65",
  "additional_information": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "bank_id": "f1ae96de-94c1-468e-93a3-6b7213930ca8",
  "created_at": "2019-08-24T14:15:22Z",
  "direction": "INCOMING",
  "expires_at": "2019-08-24T14:15:22Z",
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "ira": {
    "distribution_reason": "normal",
    "fed_withholding_amount": "102.5",
    "fed_withholding_pct": "10.25",
    "state_withholding_amount": "97.5",
    "state_withholding_pct": "9.75",
    "tax_year": "2024"
  },
  "reason": "string",
  "relationship_id": "81412018-ffa2-43f9-a3eb-d39f1c5e0f87",
  "status": "QUEUED",
  "type": "ach",
  "updated_at": "2019-08-24T14:15:22Z"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": 40010001,
  "message": "cannot submit incoming wire transfer using this API"
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-new-transfer-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successfully requested a transfer.|[Transfer](#schematransfer)|
|400|Bad Request|The request body is malformed (e.g. invalid JSON).|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|403|Forbidden|The account is not permitted to perform this transfer. Examples include:<br><br>- `deposits are not permitted for this account` — the account's `depositable_status` is not `allowed` / `limited`.<br>- `withdrawals are not permitted for this account` — the account's `withdrawable_status` is not `allowed` / `limited`.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|The request was rejected by validation. Common reasons include:<br><br>- `cannot submit incoming wire transfer using this API` — sent `transfer_type: wire` with `direction: INCOMING`. Incoming wires cannot be initiated through this endpoint.<br>- `invalid relationship_id` / `bank_id required for wire transfer` — missing the required relationship/bank identifier for the chosen `transfer_type`.<br>- `bank_id should be empty for ach transfer` / `relationship_id should be empty for wire transfer` — provided the wrong identifier for the chosen `transfer_type`.<br>- `only wire transfer type can provide additional information for the transfer` — `additional_information` was supplied on a non-wire request.<br>- `amount must be greater than 0.00` / `deposit amount must be greater than or equal to <min>` / `withdrawal amount must be greater than <min>` — amount fails the minimum-amount checks.<br>- `transfer_type must be either ach or wire` / `direction must be either incoming or outgoing` — invalid enum values.<br>|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

`POST /v1/jit/settlements`

Creates a new JIT settlement, which will trigger the reconciliation process for all included accounts. There is a limit of 150,000 accounts per settlement. If more than 150,000 accounts need to be settled, they should be batched in multiple settlements.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accounts": [
    {
      "account_number": "string",
      "amount": "string",
      "transmitter_info": {
        "originator_bank_account_number": "string",
        "originator_bank_name": "string",
        "originator_city": "string",
        "originator_country": "string",
        "originator_full_name": "string",
        "originator_postal_code": "string",
        "originator_state": "string",
        "originator_street_address": "string",
        "other_identifying_information": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "additional_info": "string",

## Retrieve Daily Trading Limits

<a id="opIdget-v1-transfers-jit-limits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/transfers/jit/limits \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/transfers/jit/limits`

The JIT Securities daily trading limit is set at the correspondent level and is used as the limit for the total amount due to Alpaca on the date of settlement. The limit in use returns the real time usage of this limit and is calculated by taking the net of trade and non-trade activity inflows and outflows. If the limit in use reaches the daily net limit, further purchasing activity will be halted, however, the limit can be adjusted by reaching out to Alpaca with the proposed new limit and the reason for the change. The limit is reset at the start of every trading day at 8.00 PM ET

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "cash_held": "20000",
  "correspondent": "EXMP",
  "daily_net_limit": "1000000",
  "executed_buys": "43140",
  "executed_sells": "0",
  "in_use_limit": "103140",
  "open_buys": "40000",
  "open_sells": "0"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-daily-trading-limits-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the JIT Securities Daily Trading Limit Object based off of real time calculations.|[DailyTradingLimit](#schemadailytradinglimit)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve JIT Reports

<a id="opIdget-v1-transfers-jit-reports"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/transfers/jit/reports?report_type=gross_summary_v2&system_date=2026-10-14' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/transfers/jit/reports`

Retrieves a JIT report for the requested report type and system date. By default, the report is returned inline. For large reports, use response_type=download_url to receive a temporary signed download URL.

Generated SDKs return the JSON response. To retrieve a report through an SDK, set response_type=download_url and download the file from `url`.


<h3 id="retrieve-jit-reports-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|report_type|query|[JITReportType](#schemajitreporttype)|true|The type of report you want to get.|
|system_date|query|string(date)|true|Date of file generation.|
|asset_class|query|string|false|The asset class to retrieve for.|
|response_type|query|string|false|Controls how the report is returned. Use inline to return the report content directly in the response. Use download_url to return a temporary signed URL that can be used to download the generated report. If omitted, the default value is inline.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|report_type|detail|
|report_type|detail_v2|
|report_type|net_summary|
|report_type|net_summary_v2|
|report_type|net_payment|
|report_type|net_payment_final|
|report_type|gross_summary|
|report_type|gross_summary_v2|
|report_type|gross_payment|
|report_type|gross_payment_final|
|report_type|obligation|
|report_type|obligation_v2|
|report_type|settlement|
|report_type|balance|
|report_type|summary|
|report_type|payment|
|asset_class|us_equity|
|asset_class|crypto|
|response_type|inline|
|response_type|download_url|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "expires_at": "2026-04-14T23:55:00Z",
  "filename": "ALPC-2026-04-14-common_stock-detail.csv",
  "url": "<signed_s3_url>"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-jit-reports-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The report file when response_type is inline or omitted, or a temporary download link when response_type is download_url.|[JITReportDownloadURL](#schemajitreportdownloadurl)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|200|Content-Disposition|string||Present when the report file is returned inline. Names the file with the same value that download_url returns in `filename`.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

## Create an instant funding request

<a id="opIdpost-v1-instant-funding"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/instant_funding \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "account_no": "string",
    "amount": "string",
    "source_account_no": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/instant_funding`

Creates an instant funding request. The request will be processed and the funds will be
made available to the account in the form of a Memopost non trade activity. Upon settlement
the Memoposted will be corrected to a CSD activity.

**Idempotency**: When the `Idempotency-Key` header is supplied, this endpoint is
idempotent. Multiple requests with the same key and identical request body will
create only one transfer. A subsequent request returns the previously created
transfer with the same response (no duplicate is created). If the same key is used
with a different request body, the API returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`.

**Recommended for production**: Always supply `Idempotency-Key` when creating
transfers. This allows safe retries on timeouts, network errors, or 5xx responses
without risking duplicate transfers. Use a client-generated unique value (e.g. UUID).


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_no": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "source_account_no": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-instant-funding-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional client-generated key for safe retries and duplicate request detection.<br>This endpoint currently accepts keys up to 128 characters. Alpaca is moving toward<br>a 36-character maximum; new implementations should generate a unique UUIDv7 or<br>UUIDv4 value (36 characters including hyphens) for each logical operation. Do not<br>reuse a key across operations.<br>|
|body|body|[CreateIFTransferRequest](#schemacreateiftransferrequest)|true|details of the instant funding request|
|» account_no|body|string|true|none|
|» amount|body|string(decimal)|true|none|
|» source_account_no|body|string|true|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "account_no": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "deadline": "1970-01-01",
  "fees": [
    {
      "amount": "string",
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "type": "partner"
    }
  ],
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "interests": [
    {
      "amount": "string",
      "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "date": "1970-01-01",
      "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "reconciled_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "status": "PENDING"
    }
  ],
  "remaining_payable": "string",
  "source_account_no": "string",
  "status": "PENDING",
  "system_date": "1970-01-01",
  "total_interest": "string"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-instant-funding-request-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Instant transfer request created.|[InstantFunding](#schemainstantfunding)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity. Returned when an idempotency key is reused with a different request body.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|default|Default|Error response.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/instant_funding/settlements \

`POST /v1/instant_funding/settlements`

Creates a new settlement, which will trigger the reconciliation process for all included
transfers and their interests. There is a limit of 50,000 transfers per settlement. If more
than 50,000 transfers need to be settled, they should be batched in multiple settlements.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "additional_info": "string",
  "transfers": [
    {
      "instant_transfer_id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "transmitter_info": {
        "originator_bank_account_number": "string",
        "originator_bank_name": "string",
        "originator_city": "string",
        "originator_country": "string",
        "originator_full_name": "string",
        "originator_postal_code": "string",
        "originator_state": "string",
        "originator_street_address": "string",
        "other_identifying_information": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Create a Journal

<a id="opIdcreateJournal"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/journals \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "amount": "115.5",
    "entry_type": "JNLC",
    "from_account": "7c891489-574f-4f9a-82f0-4082a07f4736",
    "to_account": "2d47a229-0c25-40a2-8cc7-b2c8821ff93a"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/journals`

A journal can be JNLC (move cash) or JNLS (move shares), dictated by `entry_type`. Generally, journal requests are subject to approval and starts from the `pending` status. The status changes are propagated through the Event API. Under certain conditions agreed for the partner, such journal transactions that meet the criteria are executed right away.

**Idempotency**: Reusing the same key with an identical request returns the
previously created journal without creating a duplicate. Reusing the same key with
a different request returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": "115.5",
  "entry_type": "JNLC",
  "from_account": "7c891489-574f-4f9a-82f0-4082a07f4736",
  "to_account": "2d47a229-0c25-40a2-8cc7-b2c8821ff93a"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-journal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional client-generated key for safe retries and duplicate request detection.<br>This endpoint currently accepts keys up to 128 characters. Alpaca is moving toward<br>a 36-character maximum; new implementations should generate a unique UUIDv7 or<br>UUIDv4 value (36 characters including hyphens) for each logical operation. Do not<br>reuse a key across operations.<br>|
|body|body|[CreateJournalRequest](#schemacreatejournalrequest)|true|none|
|» amount|body|string|false|Required if `entry_type` = `JNLC`|
|» currency|body|string|false|The currency of the journal. Defaults to the system currency (for example, USD in the US or EUR in the EU) when omitted. Correspondents with local currency trading enabled must send this field, and the value must be the system currency or one of the correspondent's enabled currencies|
|» description|body|string|false|Max 1024 characters. Can include fixtures for amounts that are above the transaction limit|
|» entry_type|body|[JournalEntryType](#schemajournalentrytype)|true|This enum represents the various kinds of Journal alpaca supports.<br><br>Current values are:<br><br>- **JNLC**<br><br>  Journal Cash between accounts<br><br>- **JNLS**<br><br>  Journal Securities between accounts|
|» from_account|body|string(uuid)|true|The account_id you wish to journal from|
|» qty|body|string|false|Required if `entry_type` = `JNLS`|
|» symbol|body|string|false|Required if `entry_type` = `JNLS`|
|» to_account|body|string(uuid)|true|The account_id you wish to journal to|
|» transmitter_account_number|body|string|false|Max 255 characters. See more details about [Travel Rule](https://alpaca.markets/docs/broker/integration/funding/#travel-rule) in our main documentation.|
|» transmitter_address|body|string|false|Max 255 characters. See more details about [Travel Rule](https://alpaca.markets/docs/broker/integration/funding/#travel-rule) in our main documentation.|
|» transmitter_financial_institution|body|string|false|Max 255 characters. See more details about [Travel Rule](https://alpaca.markets/docs/broker/integration/funding/#travel-rule) in our main documentation.|
|» transmitter_name|body|string|false|Max 255 characters. See more details about [Travel Rule](https://alpaca.markets/docs/broker/integration/funding/#travel-rule) in our main documentation.|
|» transmitter_timestamp|body|string(date-time)|false|RFC 3339 format. See more details about [Travel Rule](https://alpaca.markets/docs/broker/integration/funding/#travel-rule) in our main documentation.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» entry_type|JNLC|
|» entry_type|JNLS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "currency": "USD",
  "description": "",
  "entry_type": "JNLC",
  "from_account": "8f8c8cee-2591-4f83-be12-82c659b5e748",
  "id": "56f106e5-25a4-4eee-96fa-25bb05dc86bc",
  "net_amount": "1000",
  "price": null,
  "qty": null,
  "settle_date": null,
  "status": "pending",
  "symbol": null,
  "system_date": null,
  "to_account": "399f85f1-cbbd-4eaa-a934-70027fb5c1de"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
"string"
```

> 403 Response

```json
"string"
```

> 404 Response

```json
"string"
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-journal-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|The New Journal object|[Journal](#schemajournal)|
|400|Bad Request|One of the parameters is invalid.|Inline|

`DELETE /v1/journals/{journal_id}`

You can only delete a journal if the journal is still in a pending state, if a journal is executed you will not be able to delete. The alternative is to create a mirror journal entry to reverse the flow of funds.

## Create a Batch Journal Transaction (One-to-Many)

<a id="opIdcreateBatchJournal"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/journals/batch \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "correspondent": "LPCA",
    "entries": [
      {
        "amount": "string",
        "currency": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "qty": "string",
        "symbol": "string",
        "to_account": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
        "transmitter_account_number": "string",
        "transmitter_address": "string",
        "transmitter_financial_institution": "string",
        "transmitter_name": "string",
        "transmitter_timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "entry_type": "JNLC",
    "from_account": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/journals/batch`

You can create a batch of journal requests by using this endpoint. This is enabled on JNLC type Journals for now only.

Every single request must be valid for the entire batch operation to succeed.

In the case of a successful request, the response will contain an array of journal objects with an extra attribute error_message in the case when a specific account fails to receive a journal.

**Idempotency**: When the `Idempotency-Key` header is supplied, this endpoint is
idempotent. Multiple requests with the same key and identical request body will
create only one batch. A subsequent request returns the previously created
batch with the same response (no duplicate is created). If the same key is used
with a different request body, the API returns `422 Unprocessable Entity`.

**Recommended for production**: Always supply `Idempotency-Key` when creating
journal batches. This allows safe retries on timeouts, network errors, or 5xx responses
without risking duplicate batches. Use a client-generated unique value (e.g. UUID).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "correspondent": "LPCA",
  "entries": [
    {
      "amount": "string",
      "currency": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "qty": "string",
      "symbol": "string",
      "to_account": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
      "transmitter_account_number": "string",
      "transmitter_address": "string",
      "transmitter_financial_institution": "string",
      "transmitter_name": "string",
      "transmitter_timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "entry_type": "JNLC",
  "from_account": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-batch-journal-transaction-one-to-many-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|Optional client-generated key for safe retries and duplicate request detection.<br>This endpoint currently accepts keys up to 128 characters. Alpaca is moving toward<br>a 36-character maximum; new implementations should generate a unique UUIDv7 or<br>UUIDv4 value (36 characters including hyphens) for each logical operation. Do not<br>reuse a key across operations.<br>|
|body|body|[BatchJournalRequest](#schemabatchjournalrequest)|true|none|
|» correspondent|body|string|false|The 4-character correspondent code|
|» entries|body|[object]|true|An array of objects describing which accounts you want to move funds into and how much to move into each account|
|» » amount|body|string \| null|true|Journal amount in the entry's `currency`|
|» » currency|body|string \| null|false|The currency of the journal. Defaults to the system currency (for example, USD in the US or EUR in the EU) when omitted. Correspondents with local currency trading enabled must send this field, and the value must be the system currency or one of the correspondent's enabled currencies. All entries in a batch should use the same currency.|
|» » description|body|string|false|Journal entry description, gets returned in the response|
|» » qty|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » symbol|body|string|false|none|
|» » to_account|body|string(uuid)|true|The ID of the account that you want to journal funds into|
|» » transmitter_account_number|body|string|false|Only valid for JNLC journals. Null for JNLS.max 255 characters|
|» » transmitter_address|body|string|false|Only valid for JNLC journals. Null for JNLS.max 255 characters|
|» » transmitter_financial_institution|body|string|false|Only valid for JNLC journals. Null for JNLS.max 255 characters|
|» » transmitter_name|body|string|false|Only valid for JNLC journals. Null for JNLS. Max 255 characters.|
|» » transmitter_timestamp|body|string(date-time)|false|none|
|» entry_type|body|string|true|Only supports `JNLC` for now|
|» from_account|body|string(uuid)|true|The account id that is the originator of the funds being moved. Most likely is your Sweep Firm Account|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» entry_type|JNLC|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "currency": "USD",
    "description": "",
    "entry_type": "JNLC",
    "from_account": "8f8c8cee-2591-4f83-be12-82c659b5e748",
    "id": "56f106e5-25a4-4eee-96fa-25bb05dc86bc",
    "net_amount": "1000",
    "price": null,
    "qty": null,
    "settle_date": null,
    "status": "pending",
    "symbol": null,
    "system_date": null,
    "to_account": "399f85f1-cbbd-4eaa-a934-70027fb5c1de"
  }
]
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-batch-journal-transaction-one-to-many-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|an array of journal objects with an extra attribute error_message in the case when a specific account fails to receive a journal.|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Unprocessable Entity. Returned when an idempotency key is reused with a different request body.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="create-a-batch-journal-transaction-one-to-many-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[BatchJournalResponse](#schemabatchjournalresponse)]|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth

`POST /v1/journals/reverse_batch`

You can also create a batch journal request by using the following endpoint. This is enabled on JNLC for now only.

Note that if there is an invalid account_id the whole batch operation will be canceled.
Every single request must be valid for the entire batch operation to succeed.

A successful response contains an array of JNLC journal objects. If any account or entry is invalid, the whole batch operation is canceled and no per-item error result is returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "amount": "10",
      "from_account": "8e00606a-c9ac-409a-ba45-f55e8f77984a"
    },
    {
      "amount": "100",
      "from_account": "b9b19618-22dd-4e80-8432-fc9e1ba0b27d"
    },
    {
      "amount": "100",
      "from_account": "c96a5e16-7fca-425a-b67b-0814d064bfc0"
    }
  ],
  "entry_type": "JNLC",
  "to_account": "8f8c8cee-2591-4f83-be12-82c659b5e748"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-reverse-batch-journal-transaction-many-to-one-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[ReverseBatchJournalRequest](#schemareversebatchjournalrequest)|false|none|
|» entries|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » amount|body|string|false|Journal amount in the entry's `currency`|
|» » currency|body|string|false|The currency of the journal. Defaults to the system currency (for example, USD in the US or EUR in the EU) when omitted. Correspondents with local currency trading enabled must send this field, and the value must be the system currency or one of the correspondent's enabled currencies|
|» » description|body|string|false|Journal description, gets returned in the response|
|» » from_account|body|string|false|The ID of the from_account that you want to journal from|
|» entry_type|body|string|false|Only supports `JNLC` for now|
|» to_account|body|string|false|The destination of funds. Most likely is your Sweep Firm Account|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» entry_type|JNLC|

  {
    "currency": "USD",
    "description": "",
    "entry_type": "JNLC",
    "from_account": "8f8c8cee-2591-4f83-be12-82c659b5e748",

Any selling activity that takes place on or after this date will result in a corporate action entitlement.<br>- **record_date**: The date the company checks its records to determine who is shareholder in order to allocate entitlements.<br>- **payable_date**: The date that the stock and cash positions will update according to the account positions as of the record date.|

## Update the Onfido SDK Outcome

<a id="opIdpatch-v1-accounts-account_id-onfido-sdk"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/accounts/string/onfido/sdk \
  -X PATCH \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "outcome": "USER_EXITED",
    "reason": "User denied consent",
    "token": "header.payload.signature"
  }'
```

`PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id}/onfido/sdk`

This request allows you to send Alpaca the result of the Onfido SDK flow in your app. A notification of a successful outcome is required for Alpaca to continue the KYC process.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "outcome": "USER_EXITED",
  "reason": "User denied consent",
  "token": "header.payload.signature"
}
```

<h3 id="update-the-onfido-sdk-outcome-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» outcome|body|[OnfidoSDKOutcome](#schemaonfidosdkoutcome)|true|"NOT_STARTED"	The user has not started the SDK flow yet. outcome is set to this default value upon token generation<br>"USER_EXITED"	The user exited the SDK flow<br>"SDK_ERROR"	An error occurred in the SDK flow<br>"USER_COMPLETED"	The user completed the SDK flow|
|» reason|body|string|false|Any additional information related to the outcome|
|» token|body|string|true|The SDK token associated with the SDK flow you are updating the outcome for|

<h3 id="update-the-onfido-sdk-outcome-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|404|Not Found|Account Not Found|None|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid input value for outcome.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve an Onfido SDK Token

<a id="opIdget-v1-accounts-account_id-onfido-sdk-tokens"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/onfido/sdk/tokens \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/onfido/sdk/tokens`

Get an SDK token to activate the Onfido SDK flow within your app. You will have to keep track of the SDK token so you can pass it back when you upload the SDK outcome. We recommend storing the token in memory rather than persistent storage to reduce any unnecessary overhead in your app.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-onfido-sdk-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string(uuid)|true|The account ID|
|referrer|query|string|false|The referrer URL of your web app or the application ID of your mobile app. If not passed in, will default to the * wildcard|
|platform|query|string|false|Required if referrer provided. Enum values are either mobile or web|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "header.payload.signature"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-an-onfido-sdk-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Onfido applicant not yet created for account. If you haven't already contacted Alpaca to enable Onfido, please do so.|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-an-onfido-sdk-token-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|token|string|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="broker-api-rebalancing">Rebalancing</h1>

## List Portfolios

<a id="opIdget-v1-rebalancing-portfolios"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/rebalancing/portfolios \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/rebalancing/portfolios`

Lists portfolios.

When more than one query parameter is passed, only portfolios meeting all provided values will be returned (logical AND between parameter values).

<h3 id="list-portfolios-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|query|string|false|Name of portfolio|
|description|query|string|false|Description of portfolio|
|symbol|query|string|false|Symbol included in portfolio|

`POST /v1/rebalancing/portfolios`

Creates a portfolio allocation containing securities and/or cash. Having no rebalancing conditions is allowed but the rebalance event would need to be triggered manually. Portfolios created with API may have multiple rebalance_conditions, but only one of type calendar.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "cooldown_days": 0,
  "description": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "rebalance_conditions": [
    {
      "day": "string",
      "percent": "string",
      "sub_type": "string",
      "type": "string"
    }

  "weights": [

      "percent": "50",
      "symbol": "string",
      "type": "cash"
    }
  ]
}
```

|» weights|body|[[PortfolioWeightRequest](#schemaportfolioweightrequest)]|false|Weight configuration to portfolio. Sum of "percent" values in the weights array must be 100.00|

## Create Run

<a id="opIdpost-v1-rebalancing-runs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/rebalancing/runs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "account_id": "bf2b0f93-f296-4276-a9cf-288586cf4fb7",
    "type": "full_rebalance",
    "weights": [
      {
        "percent": "35",
        "symbol": "AAPL",
        "type": "asset"
      },
      {
        "percent": "20",
        "symbol": "TSLA",
        "type": "asset"
      },
      {
        "percent": "45",
        "symbol": "SPY",
        "type": "asset"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/rebalancing/runs`

Creates a rebalance run.

Omit `weights` or provide an empty array to create a subscription-driven run using the account's active subscription. Provide a non-empty `weights` array to create a manual one-off run. A manual run is rejected if the account already has an active subscription.

The determination of a run's orders and the execution of a run take place during normal market hours. Runs can be initiated outside normal market hours but remain `QUEUED` until normal market hours.

Only one run in a non-terminal status is allowed at any time.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "account_id": "bf2b0f93-f296-4276-a9cf-288586cf4fb7",
  "type": "full_rebalance",
  "weights": [
    {
      "percent": "35",
      "symbol": "AAPL",
      "type": "asset"
    },
    {
      "percent": "20",
      "symbol": "TSLA",
      "type": "asset"
    },
    {
      "percent": "45",
      "symbol": "SPY",
      "type": "asset"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-run-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» account_id|body|string(uuid)|true|The account to create the run for.|
|» amount|body|string \| number \| null|false|Optional decimal amount used by the run. JSON strings and numbers are accepted.|
|» type|body|string|true|The kind of rebalance run to create.|
|» weights|body|[[PortfolioWeightRequest](#schemaportfolioweightrequest)]|false|Asset allocation weights. Omit this field or provide an empty array to use the account's active subscription. Provide a non-empty array to create a manual one-off run. A manual run is rejected if the account already has an active subscription.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|full_rebalance|
|» type|invest_cash|

> Example responses

{
  "code": 40010000,
  "message": "request body format is invalid"
}
```

{
  "code": 40110000,
  "message": "request is not authorized"
}
```

}
```

}

## Cancel Run by ID

<a id="opIddelete-v1-rebalancing-runs-run_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/rebalancing/runs/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /v1/rebalancing/runs/{run_id}`

Cancels a run so it does not start, or is not retried. Only a run in QUEUED or IN_PROGRESS can be canceled. A run in any other status is rejected. Canceling does not stop a run that is already placing orders: those orders are not canceled, and the run's final status can replace CANCELED.

<h3 id="cancel-run-by-id-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|run_id|path|string|true|the id of the portfolio run|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 40110000,
  "message": "request is not authorized"
}
```

```json
{
  "code": 40310000,
  "message": "insufficient permission"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "code": 40410000,
  "message": "rebalance run not found"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": 40010001,
  "message": "invalid request"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": 50010000,
  "message": "internal server error occurred"
}
```

curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/rebalancing/subscriptions \

`POST /v1/rebalancing/subscriptions`

  "portfolio_id": "string"
}

<h1 id="broker-api-reporting">Reporting</h1>

## Retrieve Aggregate Positions

<a id="opIdget-v1-reporting-eod-aggregate_positions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/reporting/eod/aggregate_positions?date=1970-01-01' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/reporting/eod/aggregate_positions`

This API endpoint provides reporting data to partners for aggregate common stock and crypto positions across their account base. Partners can view historical snapshots of their holding across their entire account base. Please note that this API utilizes an 8:00 pm (EST) cutoff which aligns with the end of the Securities extended hours trading session as well as Alpaca's 24 hour Crypto trading window. Additionally, the endpoint supports indexing to help the partner efficiently filter by key information including date and symbol while being able to include or remove firm accounts.

<h3 id="retrieve-aggregate-positions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|date|query|string(date)|true|"YYYY-MM-DD" format|
|symbols|query|string|false|Comma-separated symbols. If populated, then only the specified symbols will be returned. If null, then all symbols will be included in the response.|
|firm_accounts|query|string|false|Defaults to True which includes firm accounts. Passing False will exclude all firm accounts.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "asset_type": "us_equity",
    "closing_price": "148.4700",
    "cusip": "037833100",
    "long_market_value": "148.4700",
    "long_qty": "1",
    "num_accounts": 1,
    "short_market_value": "0",
    "short_qty": "0",
    "symbol": "AAPL"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="retrieve-aggregate-positions-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Array of objects, each object pertains to the date specified in the request and a unique asset. See parameters below. Notes: Returns an empty array for non-trading days, assets with no positions are omitted.|Inline|

<h3 id="retrieve-aggregate-positions-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[[AggregatePositionResponse](#schemaaggregatepositionresponse)]|false|none|none|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve EOD Cash Interest Details

<a id="opIdget-v1-get-eod-cash-interest-report"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/reporting/eod/cash_interest \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/reporting/eod/cash_interest`

This API retrieves a list of cash interest details for the given date(s) for a single account or all accounts. End-of-day (EOD) details are typically accessible after 8:00pm Eastern Time (ET) and reflect that day's ending state across cash balances, accrued interest, accrued fees, as well as additional ancillary details.

<h3 id="retrieve-eod-cash-interest-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Account globally unique identifier. If not provided, the report will be generated for all accounts.|
|date|query|string(date)|false|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD. If not provided, the report will be generated for the most recent date this report is available.|
|after|query|string(date)|false|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD, valid only if account_id is provided and date is not provided. If not provided, this will use `before` value. If neither is provided the most recent available date is used for both `before` and `after`.|
|before|query|string(date)|false|A date in the format YYYY-MM-DD, valid only if account_id is provided and date is not provided. If not provided, this will use the most recent available date.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to use for sorting responses, either `asc` or `desc`. Only valid for account_id queries, for which only sorting by date is supported. Defaults to `desc`.|
|page_size|query|integer|false|The page size, used for paginating responses. Defaults to 1000, with a maximum of 10,000.|
|page_token|query|string|false|A token used to retrieve the next page for paginated queries. If provided the response will begin at the next page of the results for the response from which the `next_page_token` is used.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "interest": [
    {
      "account_accrued_interest": "1.2152",
      "account_id": "02e5c5ba-36d2-467a-8699-81dc24271291",
      "account_rate_bps": 423,
      "apr_tier_id": "13d149c8-d620-43e0-978b-88af8abb2ef1",
      "apr_tier_name": "gold",
      "cash_balance": "10485.76",
      "correspondent_fee": "0.0718",
      "correspondent_rate_bps": 25,
      "currency": "USD",
      "date": "2024-09-27"
    }
  ],
  "next_page_token": "293639be-8807-423f-b00d-68c781e8bb56"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-eod-cash-interest-details-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Successful response, returns a list of daily interest accruals and an optional next page token.|[EoDCashInterestReportResponse](#schemaeodcashinterestreportresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|A client error occurred. Please check the provided request parameters and try again.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized. Please check your API key and try again.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|429|Too Many Requests|Too many requests. Please wait a moment and try again.|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|A server error occurred. Please contact Alpaca.|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

## Retrieve EOD Positions

<a id="opIdget-v1-reporting-eod-positions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/reporting/eod/positions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/reporting/eod/positions`

This API retrieves a comprehensive list of end-of-day positions for all accounts. End-of-day (EOD) positions are typically accessible after 4:00 am Eastern Time (ET) on the following day, providing a comprehensive view of the day's closing positions across all accounts.
This API currently only supports retrieving EOD positions for the last trading date.

<h3 id="retrieve-eod-positions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|query|string(uuid)|false|Filter the results by account_id (optional).|
|asset|query|string|false|Filter the results by asset ID or symbol (optional).|
|asof|query|string(date)|false|The positions date in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. It's recommended to provide this parameter when the 'page' parameter is specified, to ensure precise data retrieval based on the desired date.<br>Only previous trading date is supported.|
|page_token|query|string|false|Used for pagination, this token retrieves the next page of results. It is obtained from the response of the preceding page when additional pages are available.|
|limit|query|integer|false|The number of accounts to display per page (default=1000, max=10000).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "asof": "1970-01-01",
  "next_page_token": "MTAwMA==",
  "positions": {
    "property1": [
      {
        "asset_class": "us_equity",

      }
    ],
    "property2": [
      {
        "asset_class": "us_equity",
        "asset_id": "93f58d0b-6c53-432d-b8ce-2bad264dbd94",
        "asset_marginable": false,
        "avg_entry_price": "172.08",
        "change_today": "0.0189483657034581",
        "cost_basis": "688.32",

Status Code **200**

|next_page_token|[NextPageToken](#schemanextpagetoken)|false|none|Use this token in your next API call to paginate through the dataset and retrieve the next page of results. A null token indicates there are no more data to fetch.<br>|

<h1 id="broker-api-crypto-funding">Crypto Funding</h1>

## Retrieve Crypto Funding Wallets

<a id="opIdlistCryptoFundingWallets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/wallets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}/wallets`

Lists wallets for the account given in the path parameter. If an asset is specified and no wallet for the account and asset pair exists one will be created. If no asset is specified only existing wallets will be listed for the account. An account may have at most one wallet per asset.

<h3 id="retrieve-crypto-funding-wallets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Account identifier.|
|asset|query|string|false|none|
|chain|query|string|false|Optional chain identifier. Use to request wallets for a specific chain when asset is a multi-chain crypto asset. If not specified, network is considered.|
|network|query|string|false|Deprecated. Use chain instead. Optional network identifier which is used to request wallets for a specific network when asset is a multi-chain crypto asset. When both 'chain' and 'network' are specified, 'chain' will take precedence and 'network' will be ignored. If 'chain' and 'network' are not specified, the default 'network' (ethereum) will be used.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|chain|SOL|
|chain|ETH|
|chain|BTC|
|chain|XRP|
|chain|ARB|
|network|ethereum|
|network|solana|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "string",
  "chain": "string",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-crypto-funding-wallets-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A single wallet object if an asset is specified or an array of wallet objects if no asset is specified|[CryptoWallet](#schemacryptowallet)|
|default|Default|error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
BasicAuth
</aside>

## Request a New Withdrawal

<a id="opIdcreateCryptoTransferForAccount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/wallets/transfers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "string",
    "amount": "string",
    "asset": "string",
    "chain": "SOL"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/wallets/transfers`

Creates a withdrawal request. Note that outgoing withdrawals must be sent to a whitelisted address and you must whitelist addresses at least 24 hours in advance. If you attempt to withdraw funds to a non-whitelisted address then the transfer will be rejected.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "string",
  "amount": "string",
  "asset": "string",
  "chain": "SOL"
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-new-withdrawal-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Account identifier.|
|body|body|[CreateCryptoTransferRequest](#schemacreatecryptotransferrequest)|true|none|
|» address|body|string|true|The destination wallet address|
|» amount|body|string|true|The amount, denoted in the specified asset, to be withdrawn from the user's wallet|
|» asset|body|string|true|none|
|» chain|body|string|false|Optional chain identifier. The blockchain network used for the withdrawal.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» chain|SOL|
|» chain|ETH|
|» chain|BTC|
|» chain|XRP|
|» chain|ARB|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "amount": "string",
  "asset": "string",
  "chain": "string",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "direction": "INCOMING",
  "fees": "string",
  "from_address": "string",
  "id": "497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08",
  "network_fee": "string",
  "status": "PROCESSING",
  "to_address": "string",
  "tx_hash": "string",
  "usd_value": "string"
}
```

{
  "error_code": "BENEFICIARY_NAME_REQUIRED",
  "message": "Please provide the beneficiary's name. Select one of the following options.",
  "next_actions": [
    {
      "description": "Provide the recipient's first and last name.",

          "description": "The recipient's first name.",

## Request a new whitelisted address

<a id="opIdcreateWhitelistedAddress"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://broker-api.sandbox.alpaca.markets/v1/accounts/497f6eca-6276-4993-bfeb-53cbbbba6f08/wallets/whitelists \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "string",
    "asset": "string",
    "chain": "SOL",
    "travel_rule_info": {
      "beneficiary_country_of_residence": "US",
      "beneficiary_entity_name": "Alpaca Crypto LLC",
      "beneficiary_family_name": "Doe",
      "beneficiary_geographic_address_building_number": "1",
      "beneficiary_geographic_address_country": "US",
      "beneficiary_geographic_address_post_code": "10001",
      "beneficiary_geographic_address_street_name": "Main Street",
      "beneficiary_geographic_address_town_name": "New York",
      "beneficiary_given_name": "John",
      "beneficiary_is_self_hosted": true,
      "beneficiary_manual_entry": {
        "vasp_name": "Alpaca",
        "vasp_website": "https://alpaca.markets"
      },
      "beneficiary_vasp_id": "did:ethr:0xf1c002f9e7ca88018d6dcf1e86403fb2f5f055f4"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/wallets/whitelists`

Submits a new whitelisted withdrawal address for the specified account. The chain is derived from the supplied asset symbol and address, and the same address cannot be whitelisted twice on the same chain.

Where travel rule reporting applies to the account, supply travel rule information for the destination wallet. Use the `Search VASPs` endpoint to find the VASP DID for the destination exchange. For a self-hosted wallet, set `beneficiary_is_self_hosted` to true. If the exchange is not in the directory, provide its information in `beneficiary_manual_entry`.

Note that whitelisted addresses must wait at least 24 hours before they can be used as a withdrawal destination.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "string",
  "asset": "string",
  "chain": "SOL",
  "travel_rule_info": {
    "beneficiary_country_of_residence": "US",
    "beneficiary_entity_name": "Alpaca Crypto LLC",
    "beneficiary_family_name": "Doe",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_building_number": "1",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_country": "US",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_post_code": "10001",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_street_name": "Main Street",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_town_name": "New York",
    "beneficiary_given_name": "John",
    "beneficiary_is_self_hosted": true,
    "beneficiary_manual_entry": {
      "vasp_name": "Alpaca",
      "vasp_website": "https://alpaca.markets"
    },
    "beneficiary_vasp_id": "did:ethr:0xf1c002f9e7ca88018d6dcf1e86403fb2f5f055f4"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="request-a-new-whitelisted-address-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|path|string(uuid)|true|Account identifier.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» address|body|string|false|The address to be whitelisted|
|» asset|body|string|false|Symbol of underlying asset for the whitelisted address|
|» chain|body|string|false|Optional chain identifier. Use when the underlying asset for the whitelisted address is a multi-chain crypto asset.|
|» travel_rule_info|body|[TravelRuleInfo](#schematravelruleinfo)|false|Travel rule information pertaining to the wallet being whitelisted. Identify the destination by providing beneficiary_vasp_id, setting beneficiary_is_self_hosted to true, or providing beneficiary_manual_entry. Either beneficiary_entity_name (for legal entities) or beneficiary_given_name and beneficiary_family_name (for natural persons) must be provided.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» chain|SOL|
|» chain|ETH|
|» chain|BTC|
|» chain|XRP|
|» chain|ARB|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "address": "string",
  "asset": "string",
  "chain": "string",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "id": "string",
  "status": "APPROVED",
  "travel_rule_info": {
    "beneficiary_country_of_residence": "US",
    "beneficiary_entity_name": "Alpaca Crypto LLC",
    "beneficiary_family_name": "Doe",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_building_number": "1",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_country": "US",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_post_code": "10001",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_street_name": "Main Street",
    "beneficiary_geographic_address_town_name": "New York",
    "beneficiary_given_name": "John",
    "beneficiary_is_self_hosted": true,
    "beneficiary_manual_entry": {
      "vasp_name": "Alpaca",
      "vasp_website": "https://alpaca.markets"
    },
    "beneficiary_vasp_id": "did:ethr:0xf1c002f9e7ca88018d6dcf1e86403fb2f5f055f4"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error_code": "BENEFICIARY_NAME_REQUIRED",
  "message": "Please provide the beneficiary's name. Select one of the following options.",
  "next_actions": [
    {
      "description": "Provide the recipient's first and last name.",

`PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id}/wallets/whitelists/{whitelisted_address_id}/travel-rule-info`

You are required to supply travel rule information for the crypto wallets you're withdrawing to.

It is preferred that you use the `Search VASPs` endpoint to find the VASP DID for the exchange you are withdrawing to,
otherwise, if it's a self-hosted wallet, please set `beneficiary_is_self_hosted` to true.

If the exchange cannot be found in our directory, please supply the information manually using the `beneficiary_manual_entry` object.

  }
}
