<h2 id="tocS_SignedAgreement">SignedAgreement</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasignedagreement"></a>
<a id="schema_SignedAgreement"></a>
<a id="tocSsignedagreement"></a>
<a id="tocssignedagreement"></a>

```json
{
  "account_id": "d7e8f9a0-b1c2-3d4e-5f67-890123456789",
  "agreement": "certifications_and_resolutions_statement",
  "ip_address": "10.0.0.50",
  "party_id": "e4d3c2b1-a098-7654-3210-fedcba987654",
  "revision": "01.2024.02",
  "signed_at": "2024-08-18T14:00:00Z",
  "signer_party_id": "b5c7e1a2-3d4f-4e5a-8b6c-9d0e1f2a3b4c"
}
```

A signed agreement between a party and Alpaca, as returned by
`POST /v1/agreements`. Includes both per-party and per-account agreements.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The account associated with this agreement. Present for per-account agreements<br>such as `customer_agreement`, `account_agreement`, `options_agreement`,<br>`master_securities_lending_agreement`, `crypto_agreement`,<br>`dvp_customer_agreement`, `etc_agreement`, and `joint_account_agreement`.<br>|
|agreement|[SignedAgreementType](#schemasignedagreementtype)|true|none|The type of agreement that was signed. Union of per-party and per-account<br>agreement types returned by `POST /v1/agreements`.<br><br>Per-party agreements (no `account_id`):<br>- margin_agreement<br>- certifications_and_resolutions_statement (legal entities only)<br>- nasdaq_agreement<br>- nyse_agreement<br>- oauth_api_agreement<br>- opra_agreement<br>- trusted_contact_consent<br>- custodian_customer_agreement<br><br>Per-account agreements (`account_id` present):<br>- account_agreement<br>- customer_agreement<br>- options_agreement<br>- master_securities_lending_agreement<br>- crypto_agreement<br>- dvp_customer_agreement<br>- etc_agreement<br>- joint_account_agreement<br>|
|ip_address|string|true|none|The IP address from which the agreement was signed|
|party_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The party that signed the agreement|
|revision|string|false|none|The agreement revision. The format is `XX.YYYY.MM` where XX is an incrementing<br>revision number, YYYY is the year and MM is the month. If the revision is not<br>specified in the request, the active revision will be used, which will align<br>with the [Alpaca Documents Library](https://alpaca.markets/disclosures).<br>Omitted for agreement types that do not support revisions<br>(`nasdaq_agreement`, `nyse_agreement`, `oauth_api_agreement`).<br>|
|signed_at|string(date-time)|true|none|The timestamp when the agreement was signed|
|signer_party_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The party ID of the authorized signer who signed on behalf of a legal entity.<br>Required for legal entity parties.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|agreement|margin_agreement|
|agreement|certifications_and_resolutions_statement|
|agreement|nasdaq_agreement|
|agreement|nyse_agreement|
|agreement|oauth_api_agreement|
|agreement|opra_agreement|
|agreement|trusted_contact_consent|
|agreement|custodian_customer_agreement|
|agreement|account_agreement|
|agreement|customer_agreement|
|agreement|options_agreement|
|agreement|master_securities_lending_agreement|
|agreement|crypto_agreement|
|agreement|dvp_customer_agreement|
|agreement|etc_agreement|
|agreement|joint_account_agreement|

<h2 id="tocS_SignedAgreementType">SignedAgreementType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasignedagreementtype"></a>
<a id="schema_SignedAgreementType"></a>
<a id="tocSsignedagreementtype"></a>
<a id="tocssignedagreementtype"></a>

```json
"certifications_and_resolutions_statement"
```

The type of agreement that was signed. Union of per-party and per-account
agreement types returned by `POST /v1/agreements`.

Per-party agreements (no `account_id`):
- margin_agreement
- certifications_and_resolutions_statement (legal entities only)
- nasdaq_agreement
- nyse_agreement
- oauth_api_agreement
- opra_agreement
- trusted_contact_consent
- custodian_customer_agreement

Per-account agreements (`account_id` present):
- account_agreement
- customer_agreement
- options_agreement
- master_securities_lending_agreement
- crypto_agreement
- dvp_customer_agreement
- etc_agreement
- joint_account_agreement

<h2 id="tocS_SkippedOrder">SkippedOrder</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaskippedorder"></a>
<a id="schema_SkippedOrder"></a>
<a id="tocSskippedorder"></a>
<a id="tocsskippedorder"></a>

```json
{
  "currency": "string",
  "notional": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "reason_details": "string",
  "side": "string",
  "symbol": "string"
}
```

Skipped orders model contains information for such orders that the rebalancing engine didn't send to our order system due to some validation issues.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|currency|string|false|none|Currency of the order|
|notional|string|false|none|Notional value of the order|
|reason|string|true|none|Reason for the order being skipped|

<h2 id="tocS_TimeInForce">TimeInForce</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematimeinforce"></a>
<a id="schema_TimeInForce"></a>
<a id="tocStimeinforce"></a>
<a id="tocstimeinforce"></a>

```json
"gtc"
```

The Time-In-Force values supported by Alpaca vary based on the order's security type. Here is a breakdown of the supported TIFs for each specific security type:
- Equity trading: day, gtc, opg, cls, ioc, fok.
- Options trading: day, gtc.
- Crypto trading: gtc, ioc.

Below are the descriptions of each TIF:
- day:
  A day order is eligible for execution only on the day it is live. By default, the order is only valid during Regular Trading Hours (9:30am - 4:00pm ET). If unfilled after the closing auction, it is automatically canceled. If submitted after the close, it is queued and submitted the following trading day. However, if marked as eligible for extended hours, the order can also execute during supported extended hours.

- gtc:
  The order is good until canceled. Non-marketable GTC limit orders are subject to price adjustments to offset corporate actions affecting the issue. We do not currently support Do Not Reduce (DNR) orders to opt out of such price adjustments.

- opg:
  Use this TIF with a market/limit order type to submit "market on open" (MOO) and "limit on open" (LOO) orders. This order is eligible to execute only in the market opening auction. Any unfilled orders after the open will be cancelled. OPG orders submitted after 9:28am but before 7:00pm ET will be rejected. OPG orders submitted after 7:00pm will be queued and routed to the following day's opening auction. On open/on close orders are routed to the primary exchange. Such orders do not necessarily execute exactly at 9:30am / 4:00pm ET but execute per the exchange's auction rules.

- cls:
  Use this TIF with a market/limit order type to submit "market on close" (MOC) and "limit on close" (LOC) orders. This order is eligible to execute only in the market closing auction. Any unfilled orders after the close will be cancelled. CLS orders submitted after 3:50pm but before 7:00pm ET will be rejected. CLS orders submitted after 7:00pm will be queued and routed to the following day's closing auction.

- ioc:
  An Immediate Or Cancel (IOC) order requires all or part of the order to be executed immediately. Any unfilled portion of the order is canceled. Most market makers who receive IOC orders will attempt to fill the order on a principal basis only, and cancel any unfilled balance. On occasion, this can result in the entire order being cancelled if the market maker does not have any existing inventory of the security in question.

- fok:
  A Fill or Kill (FOK) order is only executed if the entire order quantity can be filled, otherwise the order is canceled.

|qty|string|true|none|The quantity to convert for this tokenization request. It can be fractional.|
|status|[TokenizationRequestStatus](#schematokenizationrequeststatus)|true|none|Status of the tokenization request|
|token_symbol|string|true|none|The tokenized asset symbol|
|tokenization_request_id|string|true|none|Unique identifier of the tokenization request set by Alpaca|
|transfer_status|[TokenizationTransferStatus](#schematokenizationtransferstatus)|false|none|Whether Alpaca has moved the underlying shares for this tokenization request. Independent of `status`: `status` can stay `pending` until the issuer completes the on-chain mint or redeem, while `transfer_status` becomes `completed` as soon as the shares move.<br><br>- `pending`: the shares have not moved yet.<br>- `completed`: the shares have moved. Account activities can lag until after end-of-day posting.<br>- `rejected`: the share transfer failed.<br><br>Returned by the list and get tokenization request endpoints. <h2 id="tocS_TokenizationTransferStatus">TokenizationTransferStatus</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematokenizationtransferstatus"></a>
<a id="schema_TokenizationTransferStatus"></a>
<a id="tocStokenizationtransferstatus"></a>
<a id="tocstokenizationtransferstatus"></a>

```json
"completed"
```

Whether Alpaca has moved the underlying shares for this tokenization request. Independent of `status`: `status` can stay `pending` until the issuer completes the on-chain mint or redeem, while `transfer_status` becomes `completed` as soon as the shares move.

- `pending`: the shares have not moved yet.
- `completed`: the shares have moved. Account activities can lag until after end-of-day posting.
- `rejected`: the share transfer failed.

Returned by the list and get tokenization request endpoints. Omitted when Alpaca has no share transfer for the request, for example when the request was rejected during validation.

<h2 id="tocS_TradeUpdateEventType">TradeUpdateEventType</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematradeupdateeventtype"></a>
<a id="schema_TradeUpdateEventType"></a>
<a id="tocStradeupdateeventtype"></a>
<a id="tocstradeupdateeventtype"></a>

```json
"new"
```

**Common events**

These are the events that are the expected results of actions you may have taken by sending API requests.

The meaning of the `timestamp` field changes for each type; the meanings have been specified here for which types the
timestamp field will be present.

- `accepted`: Sent when an order is received and accepted by Alpaca.
- `new`: Sent when an order has been routed to exchanges for execution.
- `fill`: Sent when your order has been completely filled.
  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order was filled.
- `partial_fill`: Sent when a number of shares less than the total remaining quantity on your order has been filled.
  - `timestamp`: The time at which the shares were filled.
- `canceled`: Sent when the order transitions to the `canceled` state. This can be triggered by a user-submitted cancel request, by Alpaca as part of automated processing (e.g. corporate-action sweeps, aged-GTC expiration, overnight-session lifecycle), or by an upstream execution venue. When Alpaca populates a machine-readable cause, it is exposed on the top-level `reason` field — see the `reason` property on `TradeUpdateEventV2` for known values (e.g. `CORPORATE_ACTION`).
  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order was canceled.
- `expired`: Sent when an order has reached the end of its lifespan, as determined by the order's time in force value.
  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order expired.
- `done_for_day`: Sent when the order is done executing for the day, and will not receive further updates until the next trading day.
- `replaced`: Sent when your requested replacement of an order is processed.
  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order was replaced.

**Rarer events**

These are events that may rarely be sent due to unexpected circumstances on the exchanges. It is unlikely you will need to design your code around them, but you may still wish to account for the possibility that they will occur.

- `rejected`: Sent when your order has been rejected.
  - `timestamp`: The time at which the rejection occurred.
- `pending_new`: Sent when the order has been received by Alpaca and routed to the exchanges, but has not yet been accepted for execution.
- `stopped`: Sent when your order has been stopped, and a trade is guaranteed for the order, usually at a stated price or better, but has not yet occurred.
- `pending_cancel`: Sent when the order is awaiting cancellation. Most cancellations will occur without the order entering this state.
- `pending_replace`: Sent when the order is awaiting replacement.
- `calculated`: Sent when the order has been completed for the day - it is either `filled` or `done_for_day` - but remaining settlement calculations are still pending.
- `suspended`: Sent when the order has been suspended and is not eligible for trading.
- `order_replace_rejected`: Sent when the order replace has been rejected.
- `order_cancel_rejected`: Sent when the order cancel has been rejected.
- `trade_bust`: Sent when a previously reported execution has been canceled ("busted") by the upstream exchange.
- `trade_correct`: Sent when a previously reported trade has been corrected. For example, the exchange may have updated the price, quantity, or another execution parameter after the trade was initially reported.
- `restated`: Sent when the order is manually modified.

Represents an update to an order/trade, sent over the events streaming api.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string(uuid)|false|none|Account UUID|
|at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of event|
|event|[TradeUpdateEventType](#schematradeupdateeventtype)|false|none|**Common events**<br><br>These are the events that are the expected results of actions you may have taken by sending API requests.<br><br>The meaning of the `timestamp` field changes for each type; the meanings have been specified here for which types the<br>timestamp field will be present.<br><br>- `accepted`: Sent when an order is received and accepted by Alpaca.<br>- `new`: Sent when an order has been routed to exchanges for execution.<br>- `fill`: Sent when your order has been completely filled.<br>  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order was filled.<br>- `partial_fill`: Sent when a number of shares less than the total remaining quantity on your order has been filled.<br>  - `timestamp`: The time at which the shares were filled.<br>- `canceled`: Sent when the order transitions to the `canceled` state. This can be triggered by a user-submitted cancel request, by Alpaca as part of automated processing (e.g. corporate-action sweeps, aged-GTC expiration, overnight-session lifecycle), or by an upstream execution venue. When Alpaca populates a machine-readable cause, it is exposed on the top-level `reason` field — see the `reason` property on `TradeUpdateEventV2` for known values (e.g. `CORPORATE_ACTION`).<br>  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order was canceled.<br>- `expired`: Sent when an order has reached the end of its lifespan, as determined by the order's time in force value.<br>  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order expired.<br>- `done_for_day`: Sent when the order is done executing for the day, and will not receive further updates until the next trading day.<br>- `replaced`: Sent when your requested replacement of an order is processed.<br>  - `timestamp`: The time at which the order was replaced.<br><br>**Rarer events**<br><br>These are events that may rarely be sent due to unexpected circumstances on the exchanges. It is unlikely you will need to design your code around them, but you may still wish to account for the possibility that they will occur.<br><br>- `rejected`: Sent when your order has been rejected.<br>  - `timestamp`: The time at which the rejection occurred.<br>- `pending_new`: Sent when the order has been received by Alpaca and routed to the exchanges, but has not yet been accepted for execution.<br>- `stopped`: Sent when your order has been stopped, and a trade is guaranteed for the order, usually at a stated price or better, but has not yet occurred.<br>- `pending_cancel`: Sent when the order is awaiting cancellation. Most cancellations will occur without the order entering this state.<br>- `pending_replace`: Sent when the order is awaiting replacement.<br>- `calculated`: Sent when the order has been completed for the day - it is either `filled` or `done_for_day` - but remaining settlement calculations are still pending.<br>- `suspended`: Sent when the order has been suspended and is not eligible for trading.<br>- `order_replace_rejected`: Sent when the order replace has been rejected.<br>- `order_cancel_rejected`: Sent when the order cancel has been rejected.<br>- `trade_bust`: Sent when a previously reported execution has been canceled ("busted") by the upstream exchange.<br>- `trade_correct`: Sent when a previously reported trade has been corrected. For example, the exchange may have updated the price, quantity, or another execution parameter after the trade was initially reported.<br>- `restated`: Sent when the order is manually modified.<br>|
|event_id|string(ulid)|false|none|lexically sortable, monotonically increasing character array|
|execution_id|string(uui)|false|none|Corresponding execution of an order. If an order gets filled over two executions (a partial_fill for example), you will receive two events with different IDs.<br>Not present for `MultilegOptions`<br>|
|legs|[[TradeUpdateEventV2Leg](#schematradeupdateeventv2leg)]|false|none|Only present when event is for `MultilegOptions`. Represents filled qty/price of legs.<br>|
|order|[Order](#schemaorder)|false|none|none|
|position_qty|string|false|none|Only present when event is either `fill` or `partial_fill` other than `MultilegOptions`. The size of your total position, after this fill event, in shares. Positive for long positions, negative for short positions.<br>|
|position_qtys|string|false|none|Only present when event is either `fill` or `partial_fill` for `MultilegOptions`. The size of your total position, after this fill event, in shares. Positive for long positions, negative for short positions.<br>|
|previous_execution_id|string(uuid)|false|none|ID of the original execution that was busted or corrected (present only in trade_bust and trade_correct events).|
|price|string|false|none|Only present when event is either `fill` or `partial_fill`. The average price per share at which the order was filled.|
|qty|string|false|none|Only present when event is either `fill`, `partial_fill`, `trade_bust` and `trade_correct`. The amount of shares this Trade order was for. <br /> For `trade_bust` events, the qty field may be negative, representing a reversal of the original quantity.|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|Machine-readable code that explains **why** the event occurred. Only present when a reason applies; omitted from routine lifecycle events such as `new`, `fill`, and `partial_fill`.<br><br>Known values:<br><br>\| Value \| Event(s) \| Meaning \|<br>\| --- \| --- \| --- \|<br>\| `CORPORATE_ACTION` \| `canceled` \| Alpaca canceled the order internally because the underlying is scheduled for a mandatory corporate action other than a cash dividend (e.g. reverse split, symbol/CUSIP change, merger, liquidation). Emitted by the overnight-session lifecycle and, where enabled by Alpaca, the daytime GTC corporate-action sweep. Not emitted when the cancel is routed to the upstream venue instead (e.g. day-session, `extended_hours=false`, agency- or mixed-capacity orders); those `canceled` events carry the venue's own text in `reason` if any. \|<br>\| `TOO_LATE_TO_CANCEL` \| `order_cancel_rejected`, `order_replace_rejected` \| The cancel or replace request arrived after the order had already reached a terminal state (typically `filled`). \|<br>\| `TRADE_BUST` \| `trade_bust` \| Alpaca operations replayed or synthesized a bust of a previously reported execution. Busts that originate from the upstream venue surface the venue's own text in `reason` (or omit it entirely), so consumers should not rely on `TRADE_BUST` alone to identify all busts — key on the `event` field (`trade_bust`) for that. \|<br><br>Free-form strings may also appear in `reason`. In particular, `canceled`, `trade_bust`, and `trade_correct` events originating from the upstream venue carry the venue's own text field (when the venue provides one) rather than an Alpaca-defined code. Consumers should tolerate unknown values and, where they need to distinguish cases, key on `event` first and use `reason` as a secondary hint.<br>|
|settle_date|string(date)|false|none|Settlement date of the trade in format `YYYY-MM-DD` for `fill` and `partial_fill` events|
|swap_rate|string|false|none|Only present for `local currency trading account` or `crypto asset trade` when event is either `fill` or `partial_fill`. The swap rate at which the current trade was filled.|
|timestamp|string(date-time)|false|none|Has various different meanings depending on the value of `event`, please see the [Trading Events](https://alpaca.markets/docs/api-references/broker-api/events/#trade-events)<br>Enum in the documentation or the TradeUpdateEventType model for more details on when it means different things.<br>|

Transfers allow you to transfer money/balance into your end customers' account (deposits) or out (withdrawal).

[Main docs here](https://alpaca.markets/docs/api-references/broker-api/funding/transfers/#the-transfer-object)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|account_id|string(uuid)|true|none|The account ID|
|additional_information|string \| null|false|none|Additional information. Only applies when type = "wire".|
|amount|string(decimal)|true|none|Must be > 0.00|
|bank_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ID of the Bank, only present if type = "wire"|
|created_at|string(date-time)|true|none|Timestamp when transfer was created|
|direction|[TransferDirection](#schematransferdirection)|true|none|- **INCOMING**<br>Funds incoming to user's account (deposit).<br>- **OUTGOING**<br>Funds outgoing from user's account (withdrawal).<br>|
|expires_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when transfer expires|
|fee|string \| null(decimal)|false|none|Fee amount to be collected. Only applies when type = "wire".|
|fee_payment_method|string \| null|false|none|Either "user" or "invoice". Only applies when type = "wire".|
|hold_until|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|id|string(uuid)|true|none|The transfer ID|
|instant_amount|string|false|none|none|
|ira|[TransferIRADetails](#schematransferiradetails)|false|none|none|
|reason|string \| null|false|none|Cause of the status|
|relationship_id|string(uuid)|false|none|The ACH relationship ID only present if type = "ach"|
|requested_amount|string \| null(decimal)|false|none|Must be > 0.00. Only applies when type = "wire".|
|status|[TransferStatus](#schematransferstatus)|true|none|- **QUEUED**<br>Transfer is in queue to be processed.<br>- **APPROVAL_PENDING**<br>Transfer is pending approval.<br>- **PENDING**<br>Transfer is pending processing.<br>- **SENT_TO_CLEARING**<br>Transfer is being processed by the clearing firm.<br>- **REJECTED**<br>Transfer is rejected.<br>- **CANCELED**<br>Client initiated transfer cancellation.<br>- **APPROVED**<br>Transfer is approved.<br>- **COMPLETE**<br>Transfer is completed.<br>- **RETURNED**<br>The bank issued an ACH return for the transfer.<br>|
|type|[TransferType](#schematransfertype)|true|none|- **ach**<br>Transfer via ACH (US Only). Supports both `INCOMING` (deposit) and `OUTGOING` (withdrawal) directions.<br>- **wire**<br>Transfer via wire. `OUTGOING` (withdrawal) only.<br>|
|updated_at|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when transfer was updated|

|direction|OUTGOING|

<h2 id="tocS_UpdateOrderRequest">UpdateOrderRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaupdateorderrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_UpdateOrderRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSupdateorderrequest"></a>
<a id="tocsupdateorderrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "advanced_instructions": {
    "algorithm": "DMA",
    "destination": "IEX",
    "display_qty": "100"
  },
  "client_order_id": "61e69015-8549-4bfd-b9c3-01e75843f47d",
  "limit_price": "3.14",
  "notional": "750",
  "qty": "4",
  "stop_price": "3.14",
  "time_in_force": "gtc",
  "trail": "3.14"
}
```

Represents the fields that are editable in an order replace/update call.

Note: client_order_id is currently not editable on its own, one of the other fields must be changed at the same time to effectively replace the order.

Note: `qty` and `notional` are mutually exclusive on a single replace request. `notional` is only valid for IPO indications of interest (`asset_class: "ipo"`); non-IPO notional orders cannot be replaced at all.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|advanced_instructions|[AdvancedInstructions](#schemaadvancedinstructions)|false|none|Advanced instructions for Direct Market Access (DMA) routing. When `algorithm` is `DMA`,<br>the order is routed directly to the exchange specified in `destination`. Note that this feature is only<br>available to partners/correspondents who have been enabled for DMA.|
|client_order_id|string|false|none|A unique identifier for the new order. Automatically generated if not sent. (<= 128 characters)|
|limit_price|string(decimal)|false|none|Required if original order's `type` field was `limit` or `stop_limit`.<br>In case of `mleg`, the limit_price parameter is expressed with the following notation:<br>- A positive value indicates a debit, representing a cost or payment to be made.<br>- A negative value signifies a credit, reflecting an amount to be received.|
|notional|string(decimal)|false|none|New notional (dollar amount) for the order. Only valid for IPO indications of interest (`asset_class: "ipo"`); will be rejected for any other asset class.<br>Mutually exclusive with `qty` on the same replace request.|
|qty|string(decimal)|false|none|You can only patch full shares for now.<br><br>Qty of equity fractional orders are not allowed to change. Non-IPO notional orders cannot be replaced at all - no fields (qty, limit_price, stop_price, etc.) can be modified; cancel and resubmit instead.<br>In case of multi-leg orders represents the number of units to trade of this strategy.|
|stop_price|string(decimal)|false|none|Required if original order's `type` field was stop or stop_limit|
|time_in_force|[TimeInForce](#schematimeinforce)|false|none|The Time-In-Force values supported by Alpaca vary based on the order's security type. Here is a breakdown of the supported TIFs for each specific security type:<br>- Equity trading: day, gtc, opg, cls, ioc, fok.<br>- Options trading: day, gtc.<br>- Crypto trading: gtc, ioc.<br><br>Below are the descriptions of each TIF:<br>- day:<br>  A day order is eligible for execution only on the day it is live. By default, the order is only valid during Regular Trading Hours (9:30am - 4:00pm ET). If unfilled after the closing auction, it is automatically canceled. If submitted after the close, it is queued and submitted the following trading day. However, if marked as eligible for extended hours, the order can also execute during supported extended hours.<br><br>- gtc:<br>  The order is good until canceled. Non-marketable GTC limit orders are subject to price adjustments to offset corporate actions affecting the issue. We do not currently support Do Not Reduce (DNR) orders to opt out of such price adjustments.<br><br>- opg:<br>  Use this TIF with a market/limit order type to submit "market on open" (MOO) and "limit on open" (LOO) orders. This order is eligible to execute only in the market opening auction. Any unfilled orders after the open will be cancelled. OPG orders submitted after 9:28am but before 7:00pm ET will be rejected. OPG orders submitted after 7:00pm will be queued and routed to the following day's opening auction. On open/on close orders are routed to the primary exchange. Such orders do not necessarily execute exactly at 9:30am / 4:00pm ET but execute per the exchange's auction rules.<br><br>- cls:<br>  Use this TIF with a market/limit order type to submit "market on close" (MOC) and "limit on close" (LOC) orders. This order is eligible to execute only in the market closing auction. Any unfilled orders after the close will be cancelled. CLS orders submitted after 3:50pm but before 7:00pm ET will be rejected. CLS orders submitted after 7:00pm will be queued and routed to the following day's closing auction.<br><br>- ioc:<br>  An Immediate Or Cancel (IOC) order requires all or part of the order to be executed immediately. Any unfilled portion of the order is canceled. Most market makers who receive IOC orders will attempt to fill the order on a principal basis only, and cancel any unfilled balance. On occasion, this can result in the entire order being cancelled if the market maker does not have any existing inventory of the security in question.<br><br>- fok:<br>  A Fill or Kill (FOK) order is only executed if the entire order quantity can be filled, otherwise the order is canceled.|
|trail|string(decimal)|false|none|The new value of the trail_price or trail_percent|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|time_in_force|day|
|time_in_force|gtc|
|time_in_force|opg|
|time_in_force|cls|
|time_in_force|ioc|
|time_in_force|fok|

<!-- backwards compatibility -->

<h2 id="tocS_day_count">day_count</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaday_count"></a>
<a id="schema_day_count"></a>
<a id="tocSday_count"></a>
<a id="tocsday_count"></a>

```json
"A/360"
```

The day count convention used to calculate accrued interest.

- `A/360`: calculates the daily interest using a 360-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.
- `A/365`: calculates the daily interest using a 365-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.
- `30/360`: calculates the daily interest using a 360-day year and then multiplies that by 30 (standardized month).
- `30/365`: calculates the daily interest using a 365-day year and then multiplies that by 30 (standardized month).
- `A/A`: calculates the daily interest using the actual number of days in the year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.
- `30E/360`: number of days equals to the actual number of days (for February). If the start date or the end date of the period is the 31st of a month, that date is set to the 30th. The number of days in a year is 360.
- `B/252`: calculates the daily interest using a 252-business-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.
- `A/364`: calculates the daily interest using a 364-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|accrued_interest|number(double)|false|none|The interest that has accumulated on a bond in dollars per bond between the last interest payment and the present date that has not yet been paid to the bondholder|
|bond_status|[bond_status](#schemabond_status)|true|none|Status of the bond.|
|call_type|[call_type](#schemacall_type)|false|none|The type of call on the bond refers to one of a variety of circumstances under which a callable bond may be called.|
|callable|boolean|true|none|Whether the bond is callable, meaning the issuer has the right, but not the obligation to redeem the bond - in other words, pay out the bondholder - before its maturity date at a set price (the call price)|
|close_price|number(double)|false|none|The price of the last transaction of a security before the market closes for normal trading, shown as a percentage of par value|
|close_price_date|string(date)|false|none|The date of the close price|
|close_yield_to_maturity|number(double)|false|none|Yield to maturity of the treasury after the last close|
|close_yield_to_worst|number(double)|false|none|Yield to worst of the treasury after the last close|
|convertible|boolean|true|none|A flag indicating whether the bond is convertible|
|country_domicile|string|true|none|The country where the corporate is domiciled in the 2-alpha country code format (e.g., US, CA)|
|coupon|number(double)|true|none|The annual interest rate paid on the bond as a percentage of par value|
|coupon_frequency|[coupon_frequency](#schemacoupon_frequency)|true|none|How often the coupon is paid|
|coupon_type|[coupon_type](#schemacoupon_type)|true|none|The type of the coupon rate|
|cusip|string|true|none|CUSIP is a nine-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the security|
|dated_date|string(date)|true|none|The dated date marks the beginning of the period for which interest starts accruing on the bond|
|day_count|[day_count](#schemaday_count)|true|none|The day count convention used to calculate accrued interest.<br><br>- `A/360`: calculates the daily interest using a 360-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.<br>- `A/365`: calculates the daily interest using a 365-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.<br>- `30/360`: calculates the daily interest using a 360-day year and then multiplies that by 30 (standardized month).<br>- `30/365`: calculates the daily interest using a 365-day year and then multiplies that by 30 (standardized month).<br>- `A/A`: calculates the daily interest using the actual number of days in the year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.<br>- `30E/360`: number of days equals to the actual number of days (for February). If the start date or the end date of the period is the 31st of a month, that date is set to the 30th. The number of days in a year is 360.<br>- `B/252`: calculates the daily interest using a 252-business-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.<br>- `A/364`: calculates the daily interest using a 364-day year and then multiplies that by the actual number of days in each time period.<br>|
|description|string|true|none|Description of the corporate bond|
|description_short|string|true|none|Short description of the corporate bond|
|first_coupon_date|string(date)|false|none|The date of the first coupon payment|
|fractionable|boolean|true|none|Whether the corporate can be traded in fractional amounts|
|isin|string|true|none|International Securities Identification Number|
|issue_date|string(date)|true|none|The date on which the bond was issued|
|issue_minimum_denomination|number|true|none|The smallest unit of the bond that can be purchased at its initial offering|
|issue_price|number(double)|true|none|The price at which the bond was originally issued as a percentage of par value|
|issue_size|number|true|none|The total size amount of the bond issue in the issuing currency|
|issuer|string|true|none|The name of the issuer of the corporate bond|
|last_coupon_date|string(date)|false|none|The date of the last coupon payment|
|liquidity_institutional_aggregate|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to buy or sell (no minimum trading sizes)|
|liquidity_institutional_buy|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to buy (no minimum trading sizes)|
|liquidity_institutional_sell|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to sell (no minimum trading sizes)|
|liquidity_micro_aggregate|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to buy or sell with minimum trading sizes less than or equal to $1,000.00|
|liquidity_micro_buy|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 if the bond is priced, or null if the bond is not tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to buy with minimum trading sizes less than or equal to $1,000.00|
|liquidity_micro_sell|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to sell with minimum trading sizes less than or equal to $1,000.00|
|liquidity_retail_aggregate|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to buy or sell with minimum trading sizes less than or equal to 10,000|
|liquidity_retail_buy|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to buy with minimum trading sizes less than or equal to $10,000.00|
|liquidity_retail_sell|number|false|none|Score (from 1-5 or null if the bond is not priced/tradable) reflecting the historical depth of executable liquidity to sell with minimum trading sizes less than or equal to 10,000|
|marginable|boolean|true|none|Whether the corporate is marginable|
|maturity_date|string(date)|false|none|The date on which the bond matures|
|next_call_date|string(date)|false|none|The date of the next possible call on the bond.|
|next_call_price|number(double)|false|none|The price at which a callable bond can be redeemed by the issuer on the next call date, as a percentage of par.|
|next_coupon_date|string(date)|false|none|The date of the next coupon payment|
|par_value|number|true|none|The amount that the issuer of the bond will pay back to the bondholder upon maturity|
|perpetual|boolean|true|none|A flag representing whether a bond is perpetual|
|puttable|boolean|true|none|Whether the bond is puttable, meaning the bondholder has the right, but not the obligation to sell the bond back to the issuer at a set price (the put price) on specified dates before maturity|
|reg_s|boolean|true|none|Indicates whether the security falls under Regulation S, a rule that provides an exemption from the registration requirements for securities offerings made outside the United States|
|reissue_date|string(date)|false|none|The date on which the corporate was reissued|
|reissue_price|number(double)|false|none|The price at which the corporate was reissued as a percentage of par value|
|reissue_size|number|false|none|The total size amount of the corporate reissue in the issuing currency|
|sector|string|true|none|The sector of the corporate bond|
|seniority|string|true|none|The seniority of the corporate bond|
|sp_creditwatch|string|false|none|S&P's CreditWatch highlights S&P's opinion regarding the potential direction of a short-term or long-term rating|
|sp_creditwatch_date|string(date)|false|none|The date of the most recent Standard & Poor's CreditWatch for the bond in YYYY-MM-DD format|
|sp_outlook|[sp_outlook](#schemasp_outlook)|false|none|A Standard & Poor's rating outlook indicates S&P's view regarding the potential direction of a long-term credit rating over the intermediate term (2 years for investment grade, 1 year for speculative grade)|
|sp_outlook_date|string(date)|false|none|The date of the most recent Standard & Poor's outlook for the bond in YYYY-MM-DD format|
|sp_rating|string|false|none|Standard & Poor's rating for the bond in the standard AAA - D format|
|sp_rating_date|string(date)|false|none|The date in the timezone of the issuing country of the most recent Standard & Poor's rating for the bond in YYYY-MM-DD format|
|ticker|string|true|none|The ticker symbol of the corporate|
|tradable|boolean|true|none|Whether the treasury is tradable|
